questions: Does the five-sensor controller reproduce the iteration 0 score of about 96.8, and what is max_error on each track?
Is line_loss_events still about 1 per run on the oval and slalom, and does the s-bend still show 2 per run?
Given that all runs end off track at max_error near 0.063 m, is there any controller setting (kp, kd, or line_loss mode) you can test that would reduce max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: Map sensor_weights to the five sensors (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m). If the score is below 96.84 at this geometry, report the controller settings so I can separate geometry from control effects. If line loss persists on slalom at 12 mm, tell me whether a wider 0.016 m or edge-weighted configuration is worth one more test.

intent: Return to iteration 0's geometry, the best-scoring design (96.84), to restore a known baseline. Changes from iteration 3: sensor count back to five, sensor_size 0.012 m, forward row y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg. Expected result: a score near 96.8, with max_error near 0.063 m and line_loss_events near 1 per run on the oval and slalom. If the score matches iteration 0, the sensing and drivetrain changes since then have not helped, and the next gain must come from the controller or from a geometry change tested against this baseline.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that larger footprints (0.016 m) and a shorter look-ahead (y = 0.03 m) did not reduce line loss and lowered the score, so those changes are not the route forward. Iteration 2 showed that a 0.14 m track and 0.5 kg mass did not bring max_error below 0.06 m. The best-supported geometry is iteration 0. The open question is whether the off-track ends come from turn authority or from the controller's response. The next race should be read against the iteration 0 baseline of 96.84 on all three tracks.
rationale: Iteration 3 scored 48.12, the lowest so far, and every trial on every track still ended off track. Changing to 16 mm footprints and y = 0.03 m, together with wheel_track 0.14 m and mass 0.5 kg, made the robot worse: slalom line loss was 1.0, s-bend line loss rose to 1.25, and the scores fell on all three tracks. The 0.016 m footprint did not fix line loss, and the shorter look-ahead did not bring max_error under the 0.06 m floor. The best result remains iteration 0 (96.84), which used five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m, with wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.6 kg. Iteration 1 (seven sensors, same drivetrain) scored 91.28. Comparing iterations 0 and 1 per track, five sensors did better on s-bend (72.3 vs 63.2) and slalom (41.1 vs 31.5), and the oval was roughly equal. Iterations 2 and 3 show that the drivetrain change (0.14 m track, 0.5 kg) and the sensing change did not help. Max_error stays at about 0.063 m on every track, and the off-track floor is fixed at 0.06 m, so the next step is to return to the best-known geometry and isolate the remaining variable. I revert to iteration 0's geometry exactly: five 12 mm sensors, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, and wheel_radius and body unchanged. I expect a score near 96.8 and max_error near 0.063 m. This is a return to the best evidence, not a new gain. The Integrator will need to map sensor_weights to five sensors, and I flag that the controller must be rebuilt for this layout.
